paper_evidence.quote: Finally, we consider questions involving the class of ordered (or orderable) groups. These are special cases of both ℓ-groups (with total order) and right-ordered groups (where the order is also preserved by multiplication on the left).
3.5. Does there exist a soluble orderable group G with G/[G, G] periodic? Yes (V. V. Bludov, V. M. Kopytov, A. H. Rhemtulla [22]).
Examples of an orderable solvable group G of length three with periodic G/G' and of an orderable solvable group of length four with only one proper normal relatively convex subgroup are constructed.
An example of a solvable orderable group G such that G/G' is periodic is taken up in Sec. 4, thus answering [2, Question 5.25].
